body:
### Problem

With ui2 enabled, cancelling a prompt (`inputlist()` / default `vim.ui.select()`) while the cursor is on the last lines of a window that is scrolled to the end of its buffer moves the cursor up. With `scrolloff=3` it moves by the prompt height plus `scrolloff` (201 -> 196 below), and it is not restored when the prompt closes.

Without ui2 the cursor stays where it was.

It looks like `win_config()` in `runtime/lua/vim/_core/ui2/cmdline.lua` temporarily raises `'cmdheight'` to show the prompt; `'splitkeep'` = "screen" keeps the text in place but the bottom window still shrinks, so its cursor is moved into the smaller view (respecting `'scrolloff'`), and nothing restores it when `'cmdheight'` goes back to the user value.

### Steps to reproduce

```lua
-- repro.lua: nvim --clean -u repro.lua
vim.o.cmdheight = 0
require("vim._core.ui2").enable({})
vim.o.scrolloff = 3
vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, vim.split(("x\n"):rep(200), "\n"))
vim.cmd("normal! G")
```

1. `nvim --clean -u repro.lua`
2. `:lua vim.ui.select({ "a", "b", "c" }, {}, function() end)`
3. Press `q` to cancel
4. `:echo line('.')`

### Expected behavior

The cursor stays on line 201, as without ui2.

### Actual behavior

The cursor is on line 196.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1853+g6edb38ca98

### Operating system/version

macOS (Darwin 27.2.0)

### Terminal name/version

tmux

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-256color
